hypothesis: If the claim holds, the measured surface of a biconcave red blood cell will not have constant mean curvature.
pass_criterion: On measured 3D surface profiles of at least 50 discocytes, the standard deviation of mean curvature across the surface is > 30% of its mean, which rules out a constant-mean-curvature surface.
fail_criterion: Standard deviation of mean curvature <= 10% of its mean in most cells, consistent with a constant-mean-curvature surface.
interpretation: 'Surface of equilibrium under surface tension alone' is read as a constant-mean-curvature surface. The test is purely geometric. The proposed alternative forces (osmotic, fluid-crystal) are not tested, and modern membrane bending-elasticity theory is a reinterpretation outside the claim.
no_dataset_reason: I could not verify a specific public dataset of 3D red-cell surface geometry with a confirmed landing page and DOI, and I will not give an unverified identifier.
